samples.summary: Vacuous assertions in the "partial style" docs-tree test
samples.evidence: `expect(JSON.stringify(style)).not.toContain('undefined')` can never fail: `JSON.stringify` omits `undefined` values and serializes `NaN` as `null`, so even the pre-fix output (numeric fields = NaN, alignment = undefined) stringifies without the substring `undefined`. Likewise `expect(typeof value === 'number' ? Number.isFinite(value) : true).toBe(true)` degenerates to `expect(true).toBe(true)` for every non-numeric field. The real coverage in this test comes only from `expect(style.alignment).toBe('left')` and the `attrs` not-toHaveProperty checks; the two assertions above are presented as coverage but assert nothing.

samples.summary: Test named "omits an absent header marginFromEdge instead of writing \"undefined\"" never inspects what was written
samples.evidence: The test only reads back through `readDocsRoot` and asserts the default value, so it passes whether the writer omits the attribute or writes the literal string "undefined" (the new reader guard alone makes it green). Contrast with the block-style test above it, which does assert `expect(attrs).not.toHaveProperty('lineHeight')`. The write-side behavior the title claims is untested.

samples.summary: Slides' object-literal → Map conversions (ALGN, UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U) ship with no test of the prototype-key behavior they exist for
samples.evidence: The docs sink got an explicit `describe('DOCX_ALIGNMENTS is a closed lookup')` with `it.each(['toString','constructor',...])`. The identical hardening in slides (`ALGN` and `UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` converted to `Map` specifically so inherited keys can't reach `algn=`/`u=`) has no equivalent test: grepping packages/slides/test/export/pptx/text.test.ts for `alignment`/`underlineStyle` shows only the happy-path 'emits paragraph alignment' (center→ctr) and dashed-underline round-trip. Nothing exercises a hostile or prototype-named alignment/underlineStyle at this sink.

samples.summary: `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` cannot distinguish an explicit-undefined key from an empty object
samples.evidence: Vitest/Jest's `toHaveBeenCalledWith` uses undefined-tolerant recursive equality, so `applyStyle({})` also satisfies `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })`. The store's clearing logic (`removedInlineStyleAttrs` → `'color' in style && style.color === undefined`) depends on the key being PRESENT, which is exactly what this assertion cannot verify. The test does catch the `""` regression it targets, but not a regression to omitting the key; `expect(editor.applyStyle.mock.calls[0][0]).toHaveProperty('color')` (or `toStrictEqual`-style key check) would be needed.

samples.summary: New required-`inline.style` validation has no test
samples.evidence: The controller now rejects any inline whose `style` is not an object (`'style' must be an object` at inlines[i]), a newly-rejecting input class. The added spec only covers `inlines: [{ text: 5 }]` (the `'text'` branch) and the accepting case uses `inlines: []`, so neither the rejection of `{ text: 'x' }` (no style) nor acceptance of `{ text: 'x', style: {} }` is exercised. Searched packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.spec.ts for `inlines` assertions.

Added tests cover a malformed block inside header/footer and a non-finite `header.marginFromEdge`. Nothing covers `header: 5` (`'header' must be an object`), `header: {}` (`'header.blocks' must be an array`), or the deliberate accept-path for `header: null`/`undefined` — all new observable API responses. Searched the new spec hunk and grepped the spec for `header`/`footer`.

samples.summary: `removedCellStyleAttrs` tested only for `backgroundColor`; the nested-table claim in `removeCellNodeStyle` is only tested via colSpan
samples.evidence: `removedCellStyleAttrs` enumerates 7 keys (verticalAlign, padding, borderTop/Bottom/Left/Right too); the new tests clear only `backgroundColor`. The doc comment on `removeCellNodeStyle` specifically claims 'the fill of every nested-table cell' would otherwise be stripped, but the only nested-table assertion added is in `applyCellSpan` (colSpan). A nested-table cell fill test would be the direct proof for the applyCellStyle path.
searchedFor: read the new test hunks in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: docs-specific `""` → `undefined` reset call sites have no component-level test
samples.evidence: `docs-table-context-menu.tsx` (No-fill → `applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: undefined })`) has an existing test file `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx` which contains no `backgroundColor` assertion at all, and `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx`'s `handleTextColor(undefined)` / `handleHighlightColor(undefined)` changes have no test file anywhere (glob for *docs-formatting* under packages/frontend/tests returns nothing). Only the shared `TextFormatGroup` variant of this change is covered by the new color-reset test, so a revert to `""` in these two files would ship green.

samples.summary: PDF `styleColor` behavior changes for alpha/8-digit hex untested
samples.evidence: `styleColor` now routes through `toRgbHexColor`, which newly accepts `#RRGGBBAA` (drops alpha) and returns `undefined` for fully transparent colors. The added tests cover only `rgb(...)`, `#RGB` and the wrapped srgb form; there is no assertion for `styleColor('#11223380')` (expected 0x112233) or `styleColor('rgba(0,0,0,0)')` (expected black), so those new branches at this sink are unexercised. Searched packages/docs/test/export/pdf-style-map.test.ts.

samples.summary: Deliberate error-ordering for the cell-style check is not asserted
samples.evidence: The added code comment states the cell `style` check is placed after nested-block validation 'so the innermost problem is still the one reported'. The new test 'rejects a table cell without a style' uses `blocks: []`, so it cannot distinguish either ordering; no test supplies both a malformed nested block AND a missing cell style to pin the documented precedence.

finding.summary: The new non-finite guard in `parseBlockStyle` (the legacy-document read path) has no test
finding.evidence: `parseBlockStyle` was changed to skip attributes whose `Number(...)` is not finite, and `alignment` is now only taken when `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'`. The comment explicitly motivates this with "a document written before the serializer above" (i.e. existing CRDTs holding the literal string "undefined"). The only new test (docs-tree.spec.ts:98 'falls back to the block defaults for a partial style') exercises the WRITE path via `writeDocsRoot` with `style: {}`, which now never emits those attributes — so the read-side guard is never hit. Nothing constructs a tree whose block attrs contain `lineHeight: "undefined"`/`"abc"` and asserts the defaults come back instead of NaN.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new non-finite guard in the read path (parseBlockStyle) has no test, and specifically that "nothing constructs a tree whose block attrs contain lineHeight: 'undefined'/'abc' and asserts the defaults come back instead of NaN". That is false. docs-tree.spec.ts:139-182 ("reads a legacy poisoned block style as the block defaults") bypasses writeDocsRoot entirely and builds a raw `new Tree(...)` whose block node attributes are lineHeight: 'undefined', marginTop: 'undefined', marginBottom: 'not-a-number', textIndent: 'Infinity', marginLeft: '' (spec.ts:144-169), then calls readDocsRoot, which routes through treeNodeToBlock -> `style: parseBlockStyle(attrs)` (docs-tree.ts:457) into the Number.isFinite guard (docs-tree.ts:183-187). The assertions are non-vacuous and guard-sensitive: they compare against the real imported DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE (spec.ts:3, 173-176), which would be NaN and fail if the guard were removed, since normalizeBlockStyle is a bare spread. spec.ts:177-178 additionally pins the boundary (Number('') is 0, a finite value the reader must keep), so the test also discriminates against an over-broad guard. A parallel legacy test covers the header marginFromEdge poison path (spec.ts:206-222). The reviewer's stated grep for Number.isFinite in this file should have matched spec.ts:180, and their read stopped at line 140 — one line before the test begins. Only the `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'` sub-branch is untested, which does not sustain the filed claim that the read-side guard is never hit.
